subject: Billing cadence and temporary credit hold request — Skyward Health
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@skywardhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skywardhealth.com>, Alex Brenner <abrenner@skywardhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Quarterly invoicing + temporary credit hold for onboarding

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough. We want to proceed but need the following billing accommodations to match our fiscal cadence:

- Switch to quarterly invoicing for the first 4 invoices (we recognize this is non-standard)
- Request a temporary credit hold / one-time line of credit to cover the initial onboarding invoices while our cash timing normalizes (we're requesting $75,000)

I've attached a draft PO (PO-4591) and our internal purchase plan. This is time-sensitive for our provisioning team — they asked we lock billing before the end of the month.

Can Redwood approve a temporary quarterly remit and the credit hold while we complete our procurement checks? Happy to jump on a quick call to explain.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Procurement
Skyward Health

Attachments:
- PO-4591.pdf (pdf)
- skyward_quarterly_plan_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@skywardhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Quarterly invoicing + temporary credit hold for onboarding

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the context and the PO. Quick clarifications so I can route this for approval:

1) Is the $75k a one-time request to cover the first two quarters, or do you expect the credit to remain as an ongoing line?
2) Will Skyward sign a short amendment to the T&Cs (we can draft) that limits the concession to the onboarding period?
3) Who should our billing team coordinate with for remittance — the Procurement mailbox or Alex Brenner?

Operational note: Net-90 / quarterly invoicing exceptions require a finance sign-off and an exec discretionary approval for credit > $50k. I'm looping in Marcus from Finance and Logan from RevOps to scope the risk and timeline.

If you can confirm the answers above I’ll escalate immediately — we usually turn these around in 48–72 hours once we have the amendment and PO.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0169

Subject: Re: Request: Quarterly invoicing + temporary credit hold for onboarding

Naomi / Logan —

Reviewed Skyward's docs and PO. Summary and proposed guardrails:

- We can approve quarterly invoicing for the initial onboarding period (first 2 quarters) provided we receive a signed amendment that:
  * caps the concession to the onboarding invoices
  * acknowledges Redwood's right to revert to monthly billing thereafter
- For credit exposure: Finance can approve a temporary credit hold up to $50,000 under manager-level authority. Anything above $50k needs vp-level or exec sign-off.
- Require: signed amendment, PO (received), and a billing contact for remittance testing.

I recommend Naomi push for a 50% prepay on the initial invoice if Skyward can accommodate — that reduces exposure and speeds provisioning. If they cannot, we'll route $75k as an exec exception.

I'll add a clause to the amendment template and prepare a quick risk memo for escalation.

Marcus Lin
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Jonas —

FYI / escalation: Skyward (Strategic beta customer in the East region) is asking for a $75k one-time credit hold and quarterly invoicing for onboarding. Finance can cover up to $50k but needs exec approval for surplus.

Why I recommend exception:
- High strategic value: Skyward is an early adopter in healthcare and could drive 3 enterprise references across payer integrations.
- They committed to a 12-month minimum and provided a PO (attached).
- We can gate the concession with a signed amendment and a requirement for a 10% year-over-year price uplift at renewal.

Requesting your discretionary sign-off to approve the $75k one-time credit hold (one-time, non-recurring) conditioned on Marcus' amendment and DocuSign. If approved I will:
1) Send amendment for signature
2) Coordinate 50% prepay ask; if declined route to exec credit exception
3) Confirm billing contact and schedule provisioning once DocuSign complete

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments forwarded: PO-4591.pdf, skyward_quarterly_plan_v3.pdf
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 17:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Quarterly invoicing + temporary credit hold for onboarding

Naomi —

Approve the one-time $75,000 credit hold as a concession on the following conditions:

1) Customer signs the amendment that limits the concession to the onboarding period (first two quarters) and allows us to revert billing cadence afterward.
2) Customer commits to a 12-month term (no shorter) starting at provisioning and agrees to a 10% price step at first renewal.
3) Finance will monitor receivables and place rollback triggers if payment behavior deviates.

Please document the approval in the deal record (HubSpot DEAL-9876), attach the signed amendment, and mark this as an exec exception. Marcus, please prepare the DocuSign envelope and the brief credit memo for audit. Naomi — coordinate with Elena to close the amendment and confirm billing contact.

Jonas Weber
